name: scout
description: Repo-agnostic factory for support/investigation tooling for Claude Code teams — not a support tool itself. Developers install Scout in their repo and capture their team's tribal support knowledge as declarative 'playbooks' (YAML, no code); the resulting investigations are then consumable by ANY audience through ANY surface the repo supports — a Claude Code skill, the app's MCP server, or the app's own AI chat — so a business user with no repo access can still run a scoped, redacted investigation from the chat while a developer runs the same playbook with full evidence in Claude Code. Setup layer: /scout:setup (probe a repo — AI chat, MCP server, internal APIs, runbooks, data stores, auth/governance, and any existing investigation skills — and emit a Capability Manifest binding each abstract capability a playbook references to the repo's real endpoint/query/command + auth env var, mapping audience tiers developer/support/business/admin onto the repo's own roles so governance is inherited, not invented). Authoring layer: /scout:author (guided one-question-at-a-time wizard → one schema-validated playbook), /scout:harvest (auto-draft playbooks from existing runbooks, README troubleshooting, incident write-ups, and Makefile targets). Investigation layer: /scout:investigate (route an incoming ticket or run/record id to the matching playbook, gather evidence, emit a cited findings doc — then hand off to /agent-orch:make to fix a bug on the spot), /scout:explain (how-does-X-work from accumulated knowledge). Procedure layer: /scout:runbook (route a natural-language operation — 'promote to uat', 'sync secrets', 'refresh cache', 'run terraform apply' — to a matching kind: procedure playbook via the playbook INDEX filtered to procedures, bind its inputs, then execute its steps IN ORDER through the rails; every mutating step is needs-approval minimum with a preview + confirmation by an approval tier, followed by a verify step and rollback guidance on failure; a --dry-run mode emits a mutation-plan preview and executes nothing, and every run emits a cited run artifact). Toolbox layer (v0.4): an optional, ambient investigation_toolbox in the manifest — a shared set of common tools (app-logs, a named-allowlisted-proc db-read, traces, mcp, other) available to EVERY investigation and step WITHOUT re-declaration (still rails-gated per use), plus kind: toolbox how-to-use-a-tool playbooks composed as sub-procedures; additive and backward-compatible (absent toolbox = identical v0.3 behavior). Playbooks are JSON-Schema-validated (draft 2020-12): typed inputs, safety-classified steps (api-read/query/shell-read/skill-call/guided-human/time-travel/note), confidence-tagged conclusions, mandatory redaction, keyword/signal triggers for routing. Complements, never replaces: a step can invoke a team's EXISTING skills (investigate-sentry, custom or tool-specific investigators) and use their output as evidence, and Scout wires playbooks into the app's own AI chat / MCP so scouting enriches their decisions too. Safe-command contract enforced by construction: read-only | needs-approval | forbidden, free-form prod queries forbidden, secrets used to connect but never read/echoed, outputs redacted before any surface returns them, dry-run preview before any step runs. Complements the team-work LLM wiki when present (ingests findings, answers /scout:explain via work-ask), degrades cleanly when absent. Reuses the agent-orch extensibility contract, worktree isolation, mcp-setup, and tracker-provider patterns.
